entries.title: About Mission & Values | Banking On AI
entries.content: Skip to main content About Banking On AI Banking On AI was established to bridge the critical gap between cutting-edge machine learning innovation and the rigorous safety, governance, and auditability standards demanded by global financial regulators. Our Philosophy Governance is the Road, Not the Speed Bump: Sound risk controls and mathematical explainability do not slow innovation down—they make enterprise-scale deployment possible. Data Sovereignty & Privacy First: Financial institutions must retain absolute ownership over customer data and proprietary model weights without third-party vendor lock-in. Resilience Under Stress: Models must be evaluated not only for average accuracy during stable market regimes, but for deterministic safety during liquidity crises and systemic shocks. Research Collaborations We actively collaborate with international academic institutions, central banks, and financial industry working groups to advance responsible AI adoption frameworks. ✕ Type to search...

entries.content: Skip to main content Accessibility Statement Banking On AI is engineered to provide universal access to all visitors in accordance with WCAG 2.2 Level AAA standards. entries.title: Frequently Asked Questions | Banking On AI
entries.content: Skip to main content Frequently Asked Questions How does Banking On AI address regulatory compliance? Every architectural pattern aligns directly with established regulatory guidelines including Federal Reserve SR 11-7, OCC Model Risk Management Guidance, Basel Committee principles on operational resilience, and the EU AI Act. Can these models be deployed on-premises? Yes. All architectures support air-gapped on-premises deployment, private cloud Kubernetes clusters, and dedicated VPC enclaves ensuring zero external data leakage. How are algorithmic bias and fairness verified? We utilize statistical parity testing, equalized odds metrics, and counterfactual fairness assessments across all credit scoring and automated underwriting pipelines. How can our institution initiate an advisory engagement? Reach out through our Contact Page with an overview of your use case and timeline. ✕ Type to search...

entries.title: The Future of Banking and Finance | Banking On AI
entries.content: Skip to main content Next-Generation Financial IntelligenceEngineering Trustworthy AI for Global BankingArtificial intelligence is redefining banking. From sub-millisecond fraud detection and autonomous compliance reporting to hyper-personalized wealth intelligence, explore how AI delivers resilient, regulatory-compliant financial infrastructure.Explore Platform Talk to usBy the numbersTeams onboarded1,200+Median setup time18 minIntegrations60Uptime, trailing year99.98%One workspace, four surfaces Each surface is a full page of content on its own. The tab strip is an enhancement, not the structure. Plan Break an objective into work that fits in a week. Dependencies are declared once and drawn everywhere, so a slipped date shows up on the plan it affects rather than in someone's inbox. Build Boards, lists and a calendar over the same records. Changing the view never changes the data, so two teams can look at one backlog through the lens each prefers. Review Comments resolve against a revision rather than floating free, and an approval records who approved what, not merely that somebody did. Report Dashboards read from the same records the work lives in. There is no export step, so a number on a dashboard is never a fortnight behind the thing it describes. What you get on day oneStructured work Tasks, docs and decisions in one record type, so a search returns the decision as readily as the ticket that prompted it. Views that compose Filter, group and sort are independent. Any combination is a URL, which means a view is something you can send to a colleague. Automation you can read Rules are stated as sentences and shown in full before they run. An automation nobody can read is an outage waiting for a quiet afternoon. History that survives Every field keeps its previous values. Reverting is reading the record, not restoring a backup. Permissions by default A workspace starts closed. Sharing is a deliberate act with an audit line attached to it. Exports that round-trip What you export imports again. Leaving is supported rather than merely permitted. Built for the way teams actually split upProductRoadmaps that survive contact with a shipping date.MarketingCampaign calendars with the assets attached to the dates.OperationsRecurring work that does not depend on anyone remembering it.See all team templatesThe AI Transformation in Modern BankingThe banking industry is experiencing a profound technological transformation driven by artificial intelligence. Real-time machine learning pipelines, graph neural networks, and domain-specific large language models are replacing brittle legacy workflows with resilient, adaptive financial systems.Core Strategic Pillars1. Predictive Risk & Model GovernanceModern financial institutions deploy machine learning models under strict supervisory frameworks (including Federal Reserve SR 11-7, OCC guidance, and the EU AI Act). By integrating Explainable AI (XAI) and deterministic guardrails, banks achieve high-throughput automated decisioning while maintaining full auditability.2. Real-Time Fraud & Anomaly PreventionGraph-based machine learning analyzes transaction networks across accounts, entities, and jurisdictions in sub-milliseconds. Fraud rings, synthetic identity schemes, and money-laundering velocity spikes are neutralized before transaction settlement.3. Hyper-Personalized Client IntelligenceMachine learning transforms transactional histories into forward-looking financial advisory, cash-flow forecasting, and automated working-capital optimization for both retail customers and corporate treasuries.4. Operational Automation & Regulatory ComplianceIntelligent agents streamline high-volume compliance tasks, including ISO 20022 parsing, FinCEN filings, Basel III/IV capital adequacy reporting, and IFRS/IAS disclosure synthesis.Explore Platform See pricing ✕Type to search...

entries.title: Platform Architecture & Engineering | Banking On AI
entries.content: Skip to main content Enterprise AI Platform Architecture Banking On AI provides an architectural blueprint for deploying machine learning systems within tier-1 financial institutions with zero compromises on security, latency, or compliance. System Architecture 1. Ingestion & Event Processing Protocol Support: Native parsing for ISO 20022 XML, Swift MT/MX, FIX protocol, and real-time Kafka/Pulsar streaming telemetry. Latency Profile: Sub-millisecond stream processing with distributed memory caches. 2. Machine Learning Inference Engine Graph Neural Networks (GNNs): Dynamic account-relationship topology modeling for instant AML/KYC ring identification. Time-Series Forecasters: Multi-horizon liquidity modeling and interest rate sensitivity projections. Domain LLM Agents: Fine-tuned on financial regulation, accounting standards (IFRS 9, IAS 39), and legal credit documentation. 3. Explainability & Supervisory Audit Trails SHAP & Integrated Gradients: Instant attribution outputs generated for every algorithmic underwriting decision. Immutable Audit Logs: Cryptographically verified audit records for internal audit committees and regulatory supervisors. Sovereign Isolation: Fully deployable in private clouds, air-gapped on-premises data centers, or dedicated VPCs. ✕ Type to search...
